review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–142). It has no simp lemmas, no simp attributes, no local simp sets and no recursive definitions, and no proof uses simp. It states only subset, equality, compactness and properness theorems. Each is a one-off bridge result, and the long names are intentional. None of them is a natural canonical rewrite rule. Marking the image/closedBall equality `closedBall_eq_image_riemannianExp` as simp would be unjustified. It carries a hypothesis `hmin` that simp could not discharge, and its right-hand side would expand a closed ball into an image, which is an unwanted direction. The proofs use explicit `rw`, `exact` and term-mode lemmas, so no simp interface problem shows up. I did not read the upstream definitions of `riemannianExp` or `expDomain` in depth. I only grepped the Riemannian directory for simp attributes. The remaining uncertainty is whether other files give simp lemmas that interact with these statements, and I found no evidence of that.
